title: Kashaev volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots

decision.rationale: Selected knots and families are known, but the universal statement has no accepted proof or counterexample.

source.title: The Hyperbolic Volume of Knots from the Quantum Dilogarithm

formulation.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a hyperbolic knot and let $\langle K\rangle_N$ be Kashaev's $N$th invariant. Prove that the limit exists and satisfies
$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|\langle K\rangle_N\right|
=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K).
$$

A counterexample must give a hyperbolic knot for which the limit fails to exist or differs from the hyperbolic volume.

question.summary: Kashaev's quantum knot invariant is conjectured to grow at a rate fixed by the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement.
question.importance: The conjecture would let quantum knot invariants recover a geometric quantity of the knot complement. It links representation-theoretic data to three-dimensional hyperbolic geometry.
question.unresolved: Prove the volume-limit identity for every hyperbolic knot, or give a hyperbolic knot for which the limit fails or has the wrong value.

targetClauses.label: Universal volume-limit identity
targetClauses.text: For every hyperbolic knot, Kashaev's invariant has the stated volume asymptotic.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: Prove the identity for every hyperbolic knot, or exhibit a hyperbolic-knot counterexample.

unresolved.summary: Prove the volume-limit identity for every hyperbolic knot, or give a hyperbolic knot for which the limit fails or has the wrong value.

acceptedClaims.title: The universal hyperbolic-knot statement remains open
acceptedClaims.text: TheoremDB's dated review found proofs for selected knots and families but no proof or counterexample for every hyperbolic knot.

acceptedClaims.title: Colored Jones polynomials give an equivalent formulation
acceptedClaims.text: Murakami and Murakami identify Kashaev's invariant with a root-of-unity specialization of the colored Jones polynomial and state the volume conjecture in that language.

source.title: The Colored Jones Polynomials and the Simplicial Volume of a Knot
